long_biography.plain_text:
Lewis built parallel careers in literature and soccer. After graduating from Trinity College in 1989, he earned an MFA from the University of Virginia and taught fiction and African-American literature. His two short-story collections include I Got Somebody in Staunton, a 2006 PEN/Faulkner Award finalist whose stories examine history, race, family and place.

As a goalkeeper, Lewis played at Trinity, Virginia and with Bears FC in the Bahamas, helping the club win league and cup titles. He later coached the Bahamas national teams in Olympic and World Cup qualifying before working across all three NCAA divisions. His college posts included Colgate, Missouri S&T, Stevens Institute, Colorado School of Mines, Air Force, MSU Denver and Regis. He also founded EliteCompete to train developing and professional athletes.
